attrs.evidence: R5 wrote, in the instrument record for the kernel law suite, that a 2,000-trial property test 'is `exhaustion` with a `space_bound` of the generator's range'. That is false — QuickCheck-style property testing is random testing over generated inputs, and 2,000 draws do not enumerate a generator's range — and it is the same laundering R5 was built to stop, committed in the file that stops it. GPT-5.6 caught it. The corrected vocabulary makes the LED-C9 story exact rather than approximate: C9 had 2,000 randomized attempts at falsification, no exhaustion certificate, and no proof. `exhaustion` is now reserved for COMPLETE finite enumeration, of which this ledger has exactly one instance (REPRO-CLOSURE).
attrs.prior_art: Claessen & Hughes, QuickCheck: a lightweight tool for random testing of Haskell programs, ICFP 2000 — explicitly random testing under user-supplied generators.
attrs.statement: Randomized property testing is not exhaustion: N generated cases under a declared generator establish existence on a hit and plausibility on a miss, and never bounded absence over the generator's range.
